harness_correction.resolution: Verified pinned TS transport source: pre-dispatch errors may use mapped HTTP status; handler errors are in-band and SSE already commits HTTP 200. Corrected test oracle, preserved original results; server error behavior was unchanged.

interpretation: Validate HTTP transport, JSON-RPC envelope, and tool isError independently.
Go ProtocolVersion requests a version but permits negotiation; explicitly check InitializeResult().ProtocolVersion before relying on that revision.
Raw HTTP disconnect, Python task cancellation and Go context cancellation all caused cooperative TS handler cleanup in these probes.
A pre-recorded effect remained after cancellation; cancellation does not imply rollback.

Go emitted extra HTTP notifications/cancelled POSTs accepted with 202; Python task cancellation only closed SSE in observed traces. The spec says an HTTP cancellation notification is not required or expected. Do not teach the extra Go request as a protocol requirement.
No initialize request or MCP session ID appeared on tested current-version exchanges; an SDK object named session is not evidence of a wire session.
authInfo is trusted pass-through: application middleware verifies credentials before attaching it; SDK metadata and arbitrary headers must never supply authority.
Per-request user/tenant identity is separate from OAuth clientId. Both fixture users had the same clientId.
A principal-only private-cache key is insufficient across authorization-context changes. The fixture separated tokens and scopes as well as principal.
The private cache hint does not replace authorization; the resource scope check ran before lookup.
limitations: Only Python client -> TypeScript server and Go client -> TypeScript server were executed. No TypeScript-client, Python-server or Go-server pair was executed.
No official complete conformance suite was executed; these are bounded application-level feasibility checks.
Only loopback HTTP/SSE with deterministic tools was used; no OAuth server, production credentials, TLS, proxy or remote network.
Effects were in-memory flags. No database transaction, durable checkpoint, external effect or rollback/recovery guarantee was tested.

No stdio, MRTR continuation, optional tasks extension, subscription lifetime, legacy protocol migration or A2A runtime was tested. Private-cache authorization was checked only in the separate synthetic server fixture.
No explicit capability-mismatch, malformed output, browser-origin rejection, retry-after-lost-response, resource exhaustion or multi-process shutdown scenario was tested.
Cancellation was cooperative: the handler observed its signal and cleared its timer. A handler that ignores cancellation was not tested.
The 26-check baseline forced SSE responses. The supplemental synthetic-auth fixture exercised JSON-only responses.
Scratch source remains outside the repository. Hashes identify local artifacts; the report alone is not a complete reproducibility bundle.
Dependency versions reflect this installation on 2026-09-29; no claim that every transitive package is latest or security-audited.
Supplementary authorization tests used raw HTTP and fixed synthetic credentials; they do not establish OAuth/JWT verifier, SDK client-cache, revocation or distributed-cache conformance.

sources.purpose: Normative per-transport cancellation and timeout semantics.
Normative HTTP headers, metadata and envelope validation.
McpServer factory, createMcpHandler, toNodeHandler and localhost middleware interfaces.
Request signal and progress notification APIs.
HTTP status selection depends on error origin and response commitment.
Client mode, call_tool, progress_callback and per-round timeout signatures.
Client.Connect, ClientSessionOptions.ProtocolVersion and InitializeResult APIs; version negotiation caveat.
Context cancellation retires calls and issues an asynchronous best-effort cancellation notification.
req.auth forwarded as authInfo; authentication itself is caller responsibility.
AuthInfo clientId, scopes and extra field semantics.
Cache hints supported for cacheable operations and resource-specific overrides.
Private cache isolation by authorization context, including changed access token; cache scope is not authorization.

supplemental_test_runs.fixture: Synthetic credential lookup only; not OAuth, JWT or production-auth conformance.
supplemental_test_runs.name: synthetic-identity-handle-and-private-cache

supplemental_design.authentication: Fixed public synthetic credential strings mapped to two principals. Both users share one OAuth clientId. This is not a production verifier.
supplemental_design.authorization: Owned handle and tenant equality plus required scope checked before the effect. Resource read scope checked before cache lookup. Unavailable/denied handles produce the same response shape.
supplemental_design.cache_behavior: Two callers produce separate private entries for the same URI. Repeated same-context calls hit their own entries. A rotated token creates a third entry for the same principal. A reduced-scope token cannot access any cached value.
supplemental_design.protocol_cache_hints: resources/read returns cacheScope=private and ttlMs=30000. This does not make the SDK enforce application authorization or configure a gateway/client cache.
supplemental_design.fixture_limit: Single process, fixed authority, static private data, in-memory effect and cache. No verifier, revocation race, authz-epoch change under the same token, expiry wait, distributed cache or actual client-cache reuse was tested.
